releases.headline: This release is about noticing patterns you would otherwise have to spot yourself: where the agent had to backtrack, which prompts you keep retyping, how quickly models actually start answering, and how much Copilot agent memory has piled up on disk.

features.title: Copilot Memory Files
features.description: A new section on the Tools tab showing how much Copilot agent memory has accumulated on disk — per workspace, repo, session, and global scope — with counts for stale and oversized files so you know what is safe to clear out.

features.title: Corrections tab
features.description: Shows the moments where things went sideways — a tool call that failed, an edit the agent immediately redid, a "sorry, let me try that again" — grouped per repository. A good place to look when a session felt like hard work but you cannot say why.

features.title: Skill Suggestions
features.description: Clusters the opening prompt of your recent sessions to find the task you keep asking for by hand. Each cluster is a candidate for a reusable skill, prompt file, or custom agent.

features.title: What's New view
features.description: The last few releases in plain English, with a way in to each new view, tab, and section from here. Also where the extension sends you when it points something out.

features.title: Research → TTFT
features.description: How long each model takes to start answering you, averaged by day, week, and month with a trendline. Read straight from Copilot Chat's own debug log, so there is nothing to switch on.

releases.headline: A maintenance release: cold-boot token counts, worktree detection, and the Recent Sessions list all stopped getting things wrong. No new screens.
Two fixes for stats that under-reported: the Efficiency view no longer gets stuck after you close and reopen it, and sessions spanning midnight now count toward today.
The release that made the data comparative: efficiency over time, and per-model numbers you can rank against each other rather than read one at a time.

features.title: Efficiency view
features.description: Answers one question over the long run: are you getting more done per token than you were a month ago? Trends rather than totals.

features.title: Model Efficiency
features.description: Per-model one-shot edit rate, retry rate, cost per turn and cache hit rate in one sortable table — so "which model should I use for this" stops being a guess.

features.title: Cost by Model and Tokens by Provider
features.description: The usage chart can now be split by model or by provider, and the By Editor breakdown collapses out of the way when you are not reading it.

releases.headline: Long-context pricing became visible: the extension now knows when a request crossed into long-context rates and what that cost you.

features.title: Context Window & Long-Context Pricing
features.description: How full your context windows run, and which requests tipped into long-context pricing. Large contexts are billed differently, and this is where that shows up.
